newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rostelekom lifts Russian shares from lows.
newsitem.headline: Rostelekom lifts Russian shares from lows.

text.p: Russian shares ticked up on Friday, following telecoms company Rostelekom, which will be partly merged with telecoms holding company Svyazinvest, traders said.

Rostelekom closed on the Russian trading system at $2.58 after dropping to $2.38 in early trading from Thursday's close of $2.50. The company led the market by volume, with close to $3 million out of a total $21 million turnover.
The RTS-24 index inched up 0.28 percent to close at 188.28.
"The Rostelekom news whipped up the rest of the market," said Oleg Tatkov of Renaissance Capital.

The State Property Committee said early on Friday that there were no plans to convert the 38 percent state stake to be transferred to Svyazinvest into shares in the new company, after which the market recovered from an early drop.
After the Rostelekom stake is transferred to Svyazinvest, a stake in the merger will be sold to portfolio investors.
Traders said the market tone was firm, as shown by healthy daily market turnover volumes in the $20 millions for the last couple of weeks.
But when investors will put new money into the market is still unclear, traders said.
"The situation has not changed -- there are the same macroeconomic problems and unclarity with the International Monetary Fund tranche," which is being held up, Tatkov said.
The IMF has delayed payment of the latest tranche of a $10 billion loan on concern over the government's fulfilment of promises to reform the economy.
Oil company LUKoil failed to move sharply on news that it would offer 15 percent of the company on the New York stock exchange next year.
LUKoil common shares closed at $10.65 after $10.56 on Thursday.
Irkutskenergo firmed to $0.1155 from $0.1100. It announced that it had passed a United States Securities and Exchange Commission hurdle towards issuing an American Depositary Receipts.
